months.summary_en: The first Hijri month and one of the four sacred months. Voluntary fasting in Muharram is encouraged; Ashura falls on its tenth day.
The second Hijri month. Islam rejects the belief that Safar is inherently unlucky.
The third Hijri month. Accounts of the Prophet's birth and passing are discussed in this month, but the precise birth date is disputed.
The fourth Hijri month. Its name reflects an older seasonal naming convention; the lunar calendar moves through the seasons.
The fifth Hijri month. The expedition of Mu'tah is commonly placed in this month in 8 AH, without an established exact day.
The sixth Hijri month. Like the other lunar months, its beginning depends on the calendar convention or moon sighting used.
The seventh Hijri month and one of the four sacred months. The exact date of the Isra and Mi'raj is not reliably established.
The eighth Hijri month, immediately before Ramadan. Reports describe the Prophet ﷺ fasting frequently during Sha'ban.
The ninth Hijri month, when Muslims fast from dawn to sunset. The Qur'an describes Ramadan as the month in which the Qur'an was sent down.
The tenth Hijri month. Eid al-Fitr marks its beginning, and six voluntary fasts in Shawwal are mentioned in authentic hadith.
The eleventh Hijri month and one of the four sacred months. The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah is traditionally placed in this month.
The twelfth Hijri month and one of the four sacred months. It contains the rites of Hajj, the Day of Arafah and Eid al-Adha.
